readings.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.

devotionals.word:
The first move isn't to analyze, argue, or apply. It's to gather — to take in what the text actually says before you decide what it means. That's harder than it sounds, because we read to confirm what we already believe. Gathering is the discipline of setting that down and letting the words speak first.

The wisdom books call this the beginning, not the end: the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. "Fear" here isn't terror — it's the humility that says I don't already know this, and I'm willing to be taught. A fool, Proverbs says, despises instruction. The wise person starts by receiving.

Paul gives the same idea a different frame: a worker rightly handling the word of truth. You can't rightly handle something you haven't first picked up and looked at honestly. Right handling starts with careful handling — reading slowly, noticing what's there, and refusing to skip what's uncomfortable.

So before you study anything this year, practice the first move: read it once, slowly, and just notice what it says. Not what it means, not whether you agree — what it says. That is the whole of Gather. The rest of the method builds on nothing else.
devotionals.apply: Open to any passage — the one above will do — and read it twice. The first time, don't try to learn anything. Just name, in your own words, the plain facts of the sentence: who, what, where, when. Notice what you usually skip.
devotionals.prayer: Lord, teach me to be a receiver before I'm a critic. Slow me down, and give me the humility to let your words speak before I speak. Amen.
